title: Serverless Computing for Dynamic HPC Workflows
problem: Integrating containers with workflow management systems is complex and error-prone, hindering adoption in scientific computing. Coupling container orchestration with established workflow management systems requires significant engineering effort and complexity.
motivation: Streamlining scientific workflow execution by combining serverless abstractions with workflow management can improve resource efficiency, reproducibility, and reduce time-to-results for HPC applications.
method: Serverless platforms are integrated as an abstraction layer over container orchestrators. Serverless functions dynamically provision containers for workflow tasks based on event-driven triggers. Containers are reused across multiple workflow tasks to reduce provisioning overhead. The event-driven architecture automatically scales resources according to workflow demands.
key_novelty: Integration of serverless platforms with workflow management systems to enable dynamic container provisioning and reuse for scientific workloads.
contributions: Novel integration of serverless platforms as an abstraction layer simplifying workflow management complexity
Up to 30% performance improvement through dynamic container provisioning for workflow tasks
Demonstrates container reuse benefits across multiple tasks reducing overhead
Event-driven resource scaling aligned with dynamic scientific workload characteristics
limitations: Limitations regarding serverless cold-start overhead, platform cost implications, scalability constraints, and applicability to different scientific workflow domains are not discussed.
